title: Kudzanayi Mhlanga (Senior Vehicle Engineer · CAE AMIMI) completes Extern Externship — scores Nokia 9/20 against Incorruptible framework; proposes Quarterly Competitive Reality Review
summary: Mhlanga is a senior vehicle engineer who maintains zero-emission buses. He finished the Corporate Strategy Externship that Extern runs with Eric Ries as mentor, and applied the book's four lenses to Nokia, scoring it 9/20 and marking mission transmission the weakest lens at 2/5. He cited Vuori and Huy's 2016 work on fear among senior and middle managers, argued bad news had stopped reaching the board, and proposed a Quarterly Competitive Reality Review feeding unfiltered competitive data straight to the board's technology committee.
blockquote:
I've completed the Corporate Strategy Externship mentored by Eric Ries, run by Extern.

The work: evaluate a real company using Ries's Incorruptible framework across four lenses. Mission Drive. Financial Gravity. Governance. Mission Transmission.
My company: Nokia.
Overall score: 9/20.
Weakest lens: Mission Transmission, 2/5.

The evidence (Vuori & Huy, 2016) points to fear at the top and in middle management. Bad news stopped moving upward. The board made decisions on a filtered picture.
My recommendation: a Quarterly Competitive Reality Review reporting directly to the Board's Technology Committee. Unfiltered competitive data, on a fixed cadence, to the people who decide.

What I'm taking forward: strong results can hide structural risk. Read the governance, not just the numbers.

Day job: I maintain zero-emission buses. Same rule applies. The fault nobody reports is the one that strands the vehicle.
